_comment: Shared fixtures for the prose-block mirror pair. Read by BOTH plan-dashboard/scripts/lib/para-blocks.test.mjs and scripts/podcast/tests/test_para_blocks.py. The two halves must agree on which blocks a chapter HAS and what each is called: the Python aligner writes _system/arabic-alignment.json keyed by these fingerprints and the Composer looks paragraphs up by them, so a divergence does not degrade the Arabic reveal — it puts the wrong Arabic above the wrong paragraph.

proseBlocks._why: a blockquote is not a prose paragraph — it renders as <blockquote>, and visual-layout does not count it
headings and raw HTML blocks are excluded by the same rule
a blank line with trailing spaces still splits
a multi-line block stays ONE block
proseBlocks.in:
A sentence
wrapped over two lines.

Next.
out:
A sentence
wrapped over two lines.

proseBlocks._why: a standalone image line is not prose — it renders as a chapterImage node in the Composer, which alignablePositions does not count either; counting it here disagreed by one per image and disabled every alignment button in a chapter that had any (found 2026-08-14)
an image with alt text is still image-only, not prose
an image mid-sentence is unchanged: still literal text in a real paragraph on both sides

paraFingerprint._why: whitespace-collapsed and lowercased, so a re-wrap does not rename a paragraph
different words are a different paragraph
Arabic and its marks are part of the identity

blocksFingerprint._why: reordering two paragraphs renames the chapter's block list
a blockquote added between prose does NOT change the prose block list
